preconditions.expression: T == int(stdin.split()[0]) and T >= 1 and T <= 10
preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 10) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 3 and all(int(x) >= 1 for x in line.split()) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each of the M lines for a test case contains three integers Ai, Bi, Ci (1 ≤ Ai, Bi ≤ N, 1 ≤ Ci ≤ 10) representing a bidirectional road between intersections Ai and Bi with length Ci.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= N <= 10 and 1 <= M <= N * (N - 1) // 2 for N, M in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::M+1]])
preconditions.description: For each test case, N (2 ≤ N ≤ 10) is the number of intersections, and M (1 ≤ M ≤ N·(N–1)/2) is the number of roads. Ai ≠ Bi for all roads, and no duplicate roads exist (if i ≠ j and Ai = Aj, then Bi ≠ Bj).

preconditions.expression: all('1' in line and str(N) in line for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::M+1])
preconditions.description: The first line of each test case contains N and M, where N is the number of intersections (Tomya's house is intersection 1, Ciel's restaurant is intersection N).

postconditions.expression: stdout == ''.join(str(count_shortest_paths(N, M, roads)) + '\n' for N, M, roads in parse_test_cases(stdin))
postconditions.description: For each test case, stdout contains the number of shortest paths from intersection 1 to intersection N, where count_shortest_paths(N, M, roads) computes the count by: (1) building an adjacency list of roads, (2) finding the shortest path distance from intersection 1 to intersection N using Dijkstra's algorithm or BFS (since all edge weights are positive), (3) counting all paths from intersection 1 to intersection N whose total length equals the shortest path distance.

postconditions.expression: all(count_shortest_paths(N, M, roads) >= 1 for N, M, roads in parse_test_cases(stdin))
postconditions.description: There is at least one valid path from intersection 1 to intersection N for every test case, so the count of shortest paths is at least 1.
